prompt.brief: Design a secure multi-tier web application with isolated network zones, protected ingress, private data access, elastic capacity, strong identity controls, and auditable operations.
successSignals: Define public ingress, web, application, and data tiers with least-privilege flows, explicit trust boundaries, and no direct database exposure.
Cover TLS lifecycle, WAF/rate limits, identity propagation, secrets, patching, supply-chain controls, and administrative access.
Explain autoscaling, connection pooling, backups, multi-zone failover, idempotent mutations, and safe handling of dependency failures.
Include threat modeling, audit evidence, detection/response, observability, and a degraded mode.

functional: Serve public requests through protected ingress to stateless application services and private data stores, with authenticated user operations.
Support role-based administration, secrets/certificate rotation, audit logs, health checks, scaling policies, and controlled deployments.
Provide backups and restore tests, zone failover, rate-limit responses, replay-safe writes, and incident isolation when a tier is compromised.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 API latency under 200ms while maintaining zero direct internet access to the database tier.
Scale web and application tiers independently across multiple zones without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Secure multi-tier web application commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Secure multi-tier web application writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Secure multi-tier web application version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Secure multi-tier web application by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Secure multi-tier web application work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Secure multi-tier web application projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Secure multi-tier web application projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Secure multi-tier web application records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Secure multi-tier web application latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
